fatal_errors: The proposed SLM-plus-CALPHAD workflow does not reconstruct the target intervention of replacing EAM/TI with an MTP/FEP free-energy method.
Rapid-solidification microstructures are non-equilibrium observations and cannot directly calibrate equilibrium melting thermodynamics without additional free-energy or phase-equilibrium data.
The claimed order-of-magnitude computational improvement and increased melting-temperature accuracy are unsupported by the cited evidence.
None of the cited studies validates improved melting-property prediction from SLM-derived microstructure calibration.
explanation: The hypothesis broadly addresses HEAs and prediction efficiency, but it substitutes an experimental processing and database-calibration strategy for the target DFT-based MTP/FEP intervention. It misses the TaVCrW system, 0 GPa and 2000–2400 K conditions, MTP accuracy requirement, electronic and SRO free-energy contributions, and the quantitative FEP-versus-TI benchmark. The cited evidence supports formation of a single BCC NbMoTaW phase by SLM and the general value of high-throughput experimental validation, but not the asserted improvement in melting-temperature prediction. The proposed benchmark is somewhat falsifiable, although calibrating and testing on the same alloy risks circularity, the calibration procedure is underspecified, and DSC may be difficult for refractory HEAs. A held-out-alloy benchmark against measured solidus/liquidus values would be more decisive.
